thesis: Affirm's confirmed FQ4 2026 disclosure showed GMV growth of 36%, revenue growth of 33%, RLTC growth of 39%, and a 13% GAAP operating margin, which suggests the growth and profitability inflection is operating-led. The strongest counter-evidence is that the reported $1.6 billion of GAAP net income was boosted by releasing most of the domestic deferred-tax valuation allowance, but that does not change the long read because the GMV, revenue, RLTC, and GAAP operating-margin improvements are independent of that tax benefit.
invalidation: GMV and revenue growth decelerate materially while transaction economics or credit performance deteriorate, or the company withdraws its fiscal 2027 GAAP operating-margin outlook.

thesis: The current volume signal follows S&P Dow Jones Indices' confirmed addition of Tenable to the S&P SmallCap 600 before the August 31 open, so the setup is primarily mechanical index demand rather than fresh operating evidence. Tenable's confirmed Q2 results are credible counter-evidence—revenue grew 8.6%, GAAP operating income turned positive, and the company raised its non-GAAP full-year outlook—but those July results predate the signal and do not make one-time benchmark-tracking demand a repeatable fundamental catalyst, so the shares are avoided this run.
invalidation: After the index rebalance passes, a fresh company disclosure shows sustained organic customer and revenue acceleration rather than volume driven mainly by benchmark-tracking demand.
sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices index-addition release: https://press.spglobal.com/2026-08-26-Tenable-Holdings-Set-to-Join-S-P-SmallCap-600

thesis: Sunbelt's high volume arrives without a new completed operating catalyst and ahead of fiscal Q1 2027 results scheduled for September 9, while the latest completed fiscal-year disclosure showed 3.4% revenue growth and strong cash generation. That positive backdrop is offset by the recent confirmed accounting restatement correcting debt classification in previously issued interim statements; with the fresh evidence unresolved until earnings, this suggests avoiding the shares rather than treating the volume as a fundamental signal.
invalidation: The September 9 results confirm durable rental growth and margin resilience without further accounting-control problems or a deterioration in cash generation.

thesis: KE Holdings' confirmed unaudited Q2 2026 results showed GTV growth of 6.3% and GAAP net-income growth of 100.8%, while GAAP net revenue fell 5.7%, active-agent count contracted 7.5%, and mobile MAU declined. Transaction growth and margin expansion support a constructive long read, but the offsetting top-line and user-footprint contraction leaves the durability of the cost-led earnings improvement unresolved, keeping conviction low.
invalidation: GTV turns negative or revenue contraction persists while the gross-margin and GAAP net-income improvement fades.

thesis: Rubrik's confirmed Q2 fiscal 2027 results showed subscription ARR growth of 33%, revenue growth of 38%, positive operating and free cash flow, and raised non-GAAP full-year guidance; this suggests demand and operating leverage remain constructive. The strongest counter-evidence is Rubrik's disclosed DOJ matter: a former sales employee was indicted in October 2024 and the company found employee communications tied to potential federal-law violations involving government contracts; current growth does not erase that qualifying governance history, so the long read remains low-conviction.
invalidation: Subscription ARR or revenue growth slows materially, full-year guidance is reduced, operating cash flow turns negative, or the DOJ matter expands into charges or sanctions against Rubrik.
